name: Open USD
oneLiner: OUSD is Bridge's dollar for Open Standard, backed by cash and short Treasuries, with 1:1 business minting and redemption and no issuer fee.
collateral: Cash and short-dated U.S. Treasuries, including government money-market funds with T-bill ladders under three months. Open Standard names BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY as reserve institutions; their allocation shares are not disclosed.
pegMechanism: Bridge Building Inc. issues OUSD for the Open Standard programme, natively on Tempo, Ethereum, Base and Solana. Eligible businesses onboarded as Bridge Users mint and redeem at 1:1 USD with no issuer fee or artificial volume limits. Under the binding terms, any other holder can redeem directly only if eligible and onboarded as a Bridge User, with processing within two business days after compliance acceptance, subject to delays outside Bridge's reasonable control; holders have no property interest in reserve assets.

latestReport.reviewer: C09 bottom-up refinement 2026-10-21; EY signed report and exact four-deployment liability scope retrieved 2026-10-20; pre-launch coverage re-reviewed 2026-11-01. The August 31 examination attests only $40,690.16 of OUSD supply (Base $10,066.76, Ethereum $10,287.20, Solana $10,115.18, Tempo $10,221.02) against $40,741.77 reserves with zero timing differences. That examined supply predates the 2026-09-30 launch and equals 0.0046% of the $893,011,828.85 aggregate on-chain supply observed 2026-11-01, so the report fully reconciles a pre-launch test-scale book but does not establish whole-token liability reconciliation, which is recorded as partial. No post-launch EY report existed at 2026-11-01: the September and October monthly-named URLs return 404, the issuer dashboard links no newer report, and Bridge documents independent attestations as quarterly and optional. Open Standard's monthly-attestation promise remains unfulfilled; cadence follows Bridge's documented quarterly/optional engagement, and this pin must not be read as current whole-token assurance.

notices.title: Distinct from Origin Dollar
notices.message: Open USD is issued by Bridge for Open Standard. It shares the OUSD ticker with Origin Dollar, a separate stablecoin from Origin Protocol.

milestones.title: Open Standard unveils Open USD (OUSD), a partner-governed consortium stablecoin
milestones.description: Open Standard said more than 140 businesses had signed up to use OUSD, with launch set for later in 2026. The announcement set out no-cost minting and redemption for businesses with no artificial volume limits, and reserve earnings paid to partners less a small management fee.

milestones.title: 140+ launch partners including Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Stripe, BlackRock, Coinbase, and PayPay Corporation
Bridge co-founder Zach Abrams named interim CEO; OUSD to launch on Base, Ethereum, Solana and Tempo
Open Standard CEO essay sets OUSD economics: 'incentivize utility, not AUM'
milestones.description: Zach Abrams's post described the business model: no burn fees, a small per-transaction developer fee, and as much reserve revenue as possible shared with participating businesses, structured to reward transaction utility over assets under management. No launch date or contracts were given.

milestones.title: Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa named initial founding partners with $1B+ launch liquidity commitment
milestones.description: Open Standard named its five initial founding partners, each investing in the company and helping establish OUSD supply for more than $1 billion of near-term launch liquidity, and Zach Abrams moved from interim to full-time CEO. The announcement described equity opportunities for founders and participating partners once OUSD went live.

milestones.title: Open USD launches on Tempo, Ethereum, Base and Solana
milestones.description: Open Standard publishes the four official contracts and names Bridge as issuer. Businesses can mint and burn at a 1:1 USD conversion rate without fees; reserves are held at BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY. Monthly attestations are announced; the launch-day reserves dashboard links no independent report.
